newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila confirms ends closure on Mondragon.
newsitem.headline: Manila confirms ends closure on Mondragon.

text.p: The state-owned Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corp (Pagcor) confirmed on Friday it has withdrawn its closure order on the casino unit of Mondragon International Philippines Inc.

Pagcor said in a statement it has decided to lift its closure order after Pagcor chairwoman Alicia Reyes and Mondragon chairman Jose Antonio Gonzalez agreed to submit their differences to an arbitration committee after a meeting in the Presidential Palace in the afternoon.

"In the meantime that the dispute is being reviewed by the arbitration committee, PAGCOR will lift its notice of closure of Mondragon's operations at the Clark special economic zone; and Mondragon undertakes to stop committing the acts complained of by Pagcor," the statement said.
Pagcor said it served notice to Mondragon on Thursday that it was rescinding its licence to operate the casino due to Mondragon's "violation" of their agreement.
Pagcor, which also operates a casino near the Clark zone, accused Mondragon of poaching PAGCOR players.
